statement: For $|G|=d$, the canonical morphism of rational prounipotent groups $N^{\mathrm{un}}\to F^{\mathrm{un}}$ is surjective. Its map on abelianized Lie algebras is a surjection $\mathbb Q^{d+1}\to\mathbb Q^2$ with kernel of dimension $d-1$. It is an isomorphism exactly for $d=1$. In suitable noncanonical free pronilpotent coordinates, its Lie algebra map sends $X,Y$ to the two target generators and $z_1,\ldots,z_{d-1}$ to zero. Its kernel is the closed ideal generated by the $z_j$; by free-Lie elimination it is the completed free Lie algebra on $\mathbb Q\langle X,Y\rangle\otimes \langle z_1,\ldots,z_{d-1}\rangle$, where a word acts by iterated adjoints. Exponentiation is the exact kernel group. Every morphism from a connected unipotent rational algebraic group to the constant finite group $G$ is trivial; thus the specified map to $G$ in a kernel formula descends only for the trivial quotient. The preceding surjection is the comparison obtained from the trivial completion of $G$.
